name: Raxidi Lobo Estate - Anaerobic Natural
description:
We've been excited to collaborate with Raxidi Lobo Estate since their debut with us last year. So, when we first tasted a sample of this anaerobic natural lot, we knew it had to be a part of  Harvest '26 .   
 To bring it to life, the producers started fermenting some of the season's best cherries.  Introducing a specially curated yeast strain to the mix, they let the process go on for 48 hours. Finally, slow drying on raised beds for 21 days locked flavour.   
 Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that carries the sweet nostalgia of drinking mosambi juice in summer. It opens with berries and cherry on the nose, then settles into tart-sweet, bright notes of mosambi, green apple, and plum. The mouthfeel is velvety with a medium body, and the finish is long and tea-like.   
 Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress. 
 
  Recommended Resting Period:    11  Days

name: Kerehaklu Estate
description:
Harvest '26 debuts with a bright, citrusy light roast.  A Kerehaklu special, it shows Pranoy and Ajoy's sure hand with washed processing.  
 Ripe red Selection 9 cherries collected by seasoned pickers marked the lot's foundation. The producers then used a starter made from the farm's local microbes to aid fermentation. Monitoring temperature and pH regularly, they finished within 37 hours. Next, the coffee was mechanically washed and dried in the shade for three days. Finally, 12 days of polyhouse drying on raised beds locked its flavour. This controlled, aerobic washed process built complexity while harnessing the bean's inherent character.   
 Roasted to a light profile, the coffee delivers clean cups that open with the aroma of orange blossoms and brown sugar. Notes of orange, black tea, and green grapes follow, wrapped in a juicy mouthfeel. Expect low bitterness, medium-high acidity, and a lingering finish of orange marmalade.   
 Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress. 
  Recommended Resting Period:     12 Days  
     Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Half - Caff
description:
Our first-ever single-origin, specialty Half-Caff comes from Yelnoorkhan Estate. We selected their S795, washed processed coffee to create a complex and distinctive cup.   
 To reduce caffeine by 55%, we used CO₂ decaffeination, a chemical-free, minimal-waste generating method that is conscious in its water and energy usage. We chose it because the other decaffeination methods available to us in India came with a catch. In removing all the caffeine, they also took away the depth that makes a cup memorable. Adding artificial flavours was not something we wanted to do, never mind the fact that many of these methods also used far too much water.   
 The result is a cup with a gentler kick that holds its own in terms of flavour. You’ll first notice chocolate biscuits on the nose as well as your palate. A silky mouthfeel then reveals notes of roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish.  
 For the best experience, brew this coffee using an espresso machine. It tastes great black and is equally suited to milk-based beverages. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    5    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Sandalwood Estate
description:
This perennial coffee from 2023's harvest, Sandalwood Estate, is delicious with tasting notes of rich dark chocolate, sweet prune and zesty orange marmalade. This washed coffee, with  coffee beans  of the Sarchimor variety, was grown at a lush coffee estate in Coorg. If you’ve tried our coffees from  Attikan and Baarbara Estates , you’ll love the chocolatey flavour profile of this medium-dark roast. This heavy bodied coffee has a smooth, syrupy mouthfeel which can best be enjoyed when brewed as an Espresso, pour over or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot or French Press. The long, sweet aftertaste of butter biscuits and dried fruit come through beautifully when you allow the brew to cool down a little.   
   Recommended Resting Period:     11 Days

name: St. Joseph Estate
description:
Meet the first coffee from our newest partner farm, run by a community of Jesuit priests whose stewardship of the land spans generations.  
 A washed coffee roasted medium-dark, it opens with warm brown spice aromatics. Each sip carries a syrupy mouthfeel and reminds of grapefruit, clove, and toffee. Its medium-high body gives the cup a comforting depth, complemented by a chocolatey aftertaste.  
 Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. A versatile brew, it pairs well with milk, and holds its own black. 
  Recommended Resting Period:     10 Days
[Meta Description]: Medium-dark washed coffee with grapefruit, roasted almond, toffee, and chocolatey notes. Perfect for espresso, AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press.

name: Monsoon Malabar AA- Hoysala Estate
description:
We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala Estate. The unique flavour profile of this coffee develops when winds and humidity from seasonal monsoon rain change the characteristics of the  coffee beans . While this process has its accidental roots in colonial India when a shipment to Europe was attacked by the full force of monsoon winds, similar conditions have been recreated in a controlled environment for consistency in every lot produced.  
 When roasted medium dark, the result is a medium-bodied cup that invites with sweet aromas of butter biscuits, treating you to notes of  cocoa nib s and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate. Best enjoyed when brewed as an espresso, in the Moka Pot or the French press, the nutty flavour profile of this coffee makes for a delicious cup, either milky or black.  
  Recommended Resting Period:     15 Days
[Meta Description]: We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala Estate with butter biscuit aromas, notes of cacao nibs and dried fruit, and a dark chocolate finish.

name: Dhak Blend
description:
Our  Dhak Blend  is an ode to one of our favorite Indian trees with its colorful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring. The coffees used in this blend are naturally processed which means that the  coffee beans  are dried with the cherry, resulting in complex, fruity and sweet flavours. 
 Roasted dark to bring out flavours of dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste. 
 Our roasting team recommends the Dhak Blend for espresso-based drinks as well as manual brews such as the Moka Pot and the French Press.

name: Attikan Estate
description:
Attikan Estate's arabica  coffee beans  come from the Biligiriranga Hills in Karnataka and is make for one of our most popular coffees. Sweet with fruity overtones and balanced acidity, this is the darkest of our standard medium roasts and recommended for espresso lovers. It is a versatile coffee that also works for manual brewing such as Moka Pot, South Indian Filter and AeroPress.  
 Located to the south of Mysore, the Biligiriranga Hills, or ‘white hills’ are named after the mist that hangs over the region. At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees.

 A blend of washed and natural processed coffees, we’ve roasted it light to accentuate fruity and refreshing citrus notes. The result? Balanced cups with notes of blueberry and milk chocolate, with each sip concluding with a chocolatey finish.   
 This light and fruity favourite is best enjoyed black.

name: Mooleh Manay Estate – CM Natural
description:
Returning to our Producer Series after 2023, Komal Sable and Akshay Dashrath share their first experiment with carbonic maceration. Building on the clarity and consistency they achieved with anaerobic fermentation last season, the fifth-generation producers modified their drums to create a CO₂-rich, oxygen-free environment that allows for slower, more controlled fermentation within whole cherries.  
 The process began by removing floaters to select only ripe, dense cherries, followed by a brief pre-drying phase to reduce surface moisture. The cherries were then sealed in drums, and a custom culture was introduced to extend the fermentation. Over 60 hours, this combination of carbonic maceration and yeast inoculation ensured thorough mucilage breakdown and the development of deep complexity.  
 Post-fermentation, the cherries were dried on raised beds inside a polyhouse. Continuous raking over 7 to 10 days ensured even drying until a final moisture level of 11–12% was reached.  
 Roasted light by Rishab from our team, this coffee offers a well-structured cup with notes of fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness. It opens with the aroma of mixed berries and carries a syrupy mouthfeel, with layered flavours of dried fig, plum, black grape, and mulberry. A chocolatey aftertaste marks the finish, adding further depth.  
 We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    16  Days  
   Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

name: SKIA Coffee (Pack of 2)
description:
This two-pack (100 gms each) brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg. Grown by smallholder farmers and processed by Ashish Rao, a first-generation producer, these lots mark our first collaboration with Skia Coffee.  
 Ripe, high-density cherries were pulped with the mucilage left intact, then placed in sealed tanks for a 72-hour anaerobic fermentation. A yeast strain purpose-built for controlled fermentation was introduced during this stage to develop complexity.  
 From there, the two lots took separate paths.  
  Honey Sun Dried    
 The first lot was dried slowly on raised beds under controlled shade. Roasted to a medium profile, it makes for a balanced cup with notes of sweet lime, prunes, and almond.  
  Recommended Resting Period:  16 Days 
  Thermal Shock    
 This second lot was immersed in hot water, then rapidly cooled in ice. It was then mechanically washed and dried slowly under shade. Also roasted to a medium profile, it brews cups with notes of tangerine, brown sugar, and berries.   
 Both coffees brew beautifully as an espresso or with an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. They taste great black and pair well with milk. Together, they offer a chance to explore how thoughtful shifts in processing shape flavour in the final cup.   
  Recommended Resting Period:  12 Days 
  Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.
[Meta Description]: This two-pack brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg.

name: Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective
description:
It's always exciting for us to partner with a new farm. With Meghalaya's Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective, that excitement runs even deeper. A completely new coffee growing region for us, it speaks of the possibilities that the North East Indian soil holds for specialty production. The collective’s origin goes back a decade, when Daman, a first-generation coffee producer, visited Nongryniang—a remote village in Khasi Hills and home to the nanny who cared for him in his early years.  
 " There, nestled among the misty hills, I came across two old coffee plants growing in someone’s backyard. I later learned that back in the 1980s, the government had briefly launched a coffee planting program in the area. Like many such initiatives, it had long been abandoned and forgotten. But those plants stayed with me. And so did the people .", he recounts. Since then, Daman started a decade-long pursuit of craft and community. From shading systems to post-harvest processing, he spent years learning all it takes to grow high-quality coffee. Over time, the collective has grown in both, resolve and numbers, with 75 farmers now contributing to a harvest. They pick only the ripest cherries by hand, which are sun-dried for 15–22 days depending on weather conditions.   
 The first coffee that we’ve sourced from the collective is a natural lot we’ve chosen to roast to a medium profile. It brews cups that open with the aroma of raisins, unfolding into a creamy mouthfeel. Notes of blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish. A balanced coffee, it lends well to various brewing methods, including espresso, Moka Pot, French Press, and AeroPress. It is enjoyable on its own as well as in milk-based beverages. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    13  Days
[Meta Description]: Discover our newest partner, Meghalaya’s Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective as we explore the rich potential of North East India’s soil for specialty coffee production.

name: Ratnagiri Estate - Dark Room Natural
description:
Our latest release from Ratnagiri Estate showcases a new frontier in controlled processing. It was shaped by a 60-hour fermentation with a custom culture, then dried slowly for 13 days in the estate’s climate-controlled dark room. 
 A rare facility found at only a handful of estates worldwide, the dark room is fully sealed and fitted with precision racks. It holds temperature between 2°C and 30°C and maintains humidity at 10%. Slow drying with this level of control deepens flavour, preserves sweetness, and brings clarity to the cup. 
 Antony, our roaster, approached the roast with a carefully extended Maillard phase to build natural sweetness, finishing light to let the coffee’s character shine. The result is a sparkling wine-like cup with a silky body and a bright mouthfeel. It opens with the aroma of strawberry and prune. Notes of passionfruit, mosambi, pineapple, and black tea follow, with the tea-like note carrying through the finish. 
 For the best experience, we suggest brewing this limited-edition lot as a Pour Over or using an AeroPress. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    8    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Kalledevarapura Estate - The Fermentation Edit
description:
Meet our roasters’ favourite experiment from Nano-X ’25. 
 To create this special five-pack, we played with a whole spectrum of microorganisms, from homegrown kombucha to lab-cultured strains. Working with a local laboratory, the producer, Shravan, curated a diverse range of cultures, while Tyler, our Head of Roastery, prepared a robust batch of active kombucha using black tea and raw sugar. 
 Ripe coffee cherries were split into eleven barrels of 120 kg each, with inoculants gradually added to ten barrels while one was kept as a control. The barrels were sealed and left indoors for a 72-hour fermentation, with the kombucha batch opened after 24 hours to allow oxygen exposure, as the SCOBY (Symbiotic Culture of Bacteria and Yeast) requires it to remain active. Once fermentation was complete, the cherries were dried on raised beds for 20 to 25 days. 
 This limited-release brings together the highest-scoring samples from the experiment. It includes lots fermented with: 
 Homegrown Kombucha, creating a cup with notes of plum, raw mango, candy apple, and goji berries. 
 Saccharomyces cerevisiae, building an expressive coffee with notes of white nectarine, pomegranate, roasted hazelnut, and pomelo. 
 Pichia yeast, developing a clean cup with notes of cane sugar, green apple, jaggery, and roasted almonds. 
 Lactic acid bacteria, which shaped a coffee with notes of orange zest, black raisin, wild honey, and cocoa. 
 An anaerobically processed natural, used to benchmark the inoculated lots. It brews cups with hints of florality and notes of lemonade, roasted almond, and green grape. 
 We recommend drinking these coffees black, brewed as Pour Overs or using the AeroPress. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    12    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Riverdale Estate - White Rose
description:
Fermented with rose petals, this layered light roast perfectly embodies why Riverdale Estate is a pioneer in experimental processing. 
 Only the ripest cherries, hand-picked from the higher-altitude blocks of the farm, where the fruit matures slowly and develops an enhanced sweetness, were used. Once harvested, the cherries underwent a triple wash with natural spring water to remove impurities. 
 After removing floaters, rose petals were introduced during fermentation, setting up the stage for complexity. The cherries were then slow-dried on raised beds for up to 30 days, allowing for even drying. Finally, the coffee was hulled at the estate’s dry mill, where any defective beans were eliminated before being sent to our roastery. 
 The result is a gently perfumed cup with bright notes of plum, pomegranate, strawberry and orange blossom, complemented by a smooth mouthfeel and a lingering sweetness. 
 We recommend brewing it black using an AeroPress or as a Pour Over. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    14  Days  
     Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Winter Blend
description:
Meet the blend our roasters look forward to crafting each winter. Pairing well with milk, it is also a solid base for all those winter recipes you've been saving. 
 We've created it using a careful mix of natural and washed lots from St. Joseph Estate and Attikan Estate. Opening with the aroma of brown spices, this coffee has a medium body and a syrupy, round mouthfeel. You’ll be able to taste cinnamon, cacao, roasted almonds, and raisins, and tying everything together nicely is a chocolatey aftertaste. 
 We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or with a Moka Pot or French Press. 
  Recommended Resting Period:  10 Days

name: Krishnagiri Estate
description:
A single origin dark roast, this coffee comes from a Rainforest Alliance Certified farm. The producers used a custom-designed pulper to process this washed lot, minimising water usage.   
 In the cup, you'll first notice the aroma of brown spices. The brew, characterised by mellow acidity, a heavy body, and a velvety mouthfeel, reminds of oak, toasted walnuts, and malt. A bittersweet finish lingers between sips.   
 We recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, using a Moka Pot, French Press, or an AeroPress. It is rich enough to enjoy black, and also pairs well with milk. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    7  Days
